correctness.rationale: The invariant simplex yields global existence; logistic comparison bounds total infection away from zero and a differential inequality bounds susceptible mass away from zero. Exact weighted-infection difference and log-ratio equations preserve all strict ranks and tied classes and drive every loser to zero exponentially. A unique positive scalar root controls the selected-support equilibrium, and its Jacobian has the stated eigenvalues. Cesaro averaging of an explicitly convergent log-ratio derivative gives the exact physical-time elimination exponent. Dirichlet-exponential representation and inclusion-exclusion give the seed probabilities. The standalone program passed 12,600 rational pair identities, 4,424 exact Jacobian/probability checks, and 67 numerical trajectories; the proof is independent of finite experiments.

originality.rationale: Inspected Li et al. arXiv:2105.08234v1 equations and phase analysis, Gracy et al. arXiv:2309.14230v1 networked bivirus model, and relevant single-pathogen higher-order literature. Available published-result searches and the recoverable preceding ledger claims found no direct or stronger theorem simultaneously implying arbitrary-m exact gamma_i x_i seed basins, epidemic-size and time-rate constants, and the Dirichlet winner law. Nevertheless the normalized dynamics equal a diagonal replicator time change; prior diagonal coordination-game basin classifications may imply much of the composition result and remain a documented priority risk.
residual_risks: The normalized composition is an exact positive time-change of a standard diagonal-payoff replicator equation; a prior explicit global basin classification could imply a large portion of this contribution. No claim of new general replicator theory is made.
Updated 2026 journal treatment of the competing networked bivirus problem was not exhaustively inspected; the arXiv 2023 preprint was inspected.

The probabilistic inclusion-exclusion identity for independent exponential variables is a classical probability calculation; its contribution is its exact application to the model-specific seeded winner criterion.

value.rationale: Li et al. study initial-condition-dependent competitive dominance in simplicial SIS without a complete global seed selection criterion. An all-m, all-initial partition by reinforcement-weighted prevalence, exact tie/coexistence boundaries, endemic fractions, quantitative physical-time extinction of losers, and an explicit inoculum winner distribution together resolve a natural applied modeling question. The result is a complete parameterized structural outcome theorem, not a routine new finite cutoff; the diagonal-replicator equivalence and restricted common-rate assumptions are explicitly stated.
